newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel names Euro allies for Thomson.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel names Euro allies for Thomson.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk said on Tuesday that he aimed to conclude deals with both Germany's DASA and Britain's GEC Plc in defence activities if it won the bidding for Thomson-CSF.

Alcatel, together with Dassault Industries, and Lagardere Groupe are the declared candidates for buying a 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF from the state. The deadline for candidates closes on March 28 and the state aims to declare the winner by June 30.
Tchuruk told a news conference his bid with Dassault would also involve state-owned Aerospatiale.
The government said last week that Aerospatiale could not participate itself in the bidding for Thomson-CSF by allying itself to one candidate or another.
"The project, as we have presented it, is a joint project with Dassault, Alcatel being the syndicate leader, the main shareholder in the plans," Tchuruk said.
"Aerospatiale plays an integral part in these plans .... Aerospatiale will have a stake in Thomson," he said.

"If we succeed in obtaining the deal, we would be very keen in building European cooperation. We have, of course, had discussions with DASA and GEC. That being said, the game is entirely open," he added.
Asked whether Alcatel had obtained firm commitments from DASA or GEC, Tchuruk said he was not seeking such commitments.

"I have excellent relationships with GEC and with DASA, but it is already difficult to mount a precise deal with two or three French parties. To then make it more complex with preliminarly agreements before obtaining the deal...," he said.

He said that while in the U.S. a big wave of restructuring was going on, in Europe the defence industry was shattered due to national interest and had led to a number of joint venture deals in which "nobody is the boss".
He said he hoped to be able to find middle ground between the U.S. and European models.
Alcatel presented a glossy brochure after the results news conference detailing its plans with Thomson-CSF.
It said the joint operatrion would create a defence group with annual sales of 60 billion francs ($10.5 billion), with four main activities.
In defence electronics, Dassault Electronique would be merged with the electronics activities of Thomson-CSF which would create the biggest European group in radars and counter-measures.
In military communications, a combination of Thomson-CSF and Alcatel would create a world sector leader.

In satellites, a combination of Thomson-CSF, Alcatel and Aerospatiale would create a European giant with 10 billion francs in sales rivalling the seven billion francs Matra Marconi Space venture of Lagardere and GEC Plc.

In missiles, the combination of Aerospatiale and Thomson-CSF would create a seven billion franc entity capable of rivalling Matra British Aerospace Dymanics -- an eight billion franc sales joint venture of Matra and British Aerospace.
Alcatel said that in a second stage, the missiles activities of DASA could also be included.
The new Thomson-CSF combination would employ 60,000 people in Europe, Alcatel said.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.704 French Francs)
